decisions.statement: Nothing here ends the process.
An exit the worker should make is answered to the caller.
An exit answered has the code the worker should end on.
An exit answered has the reason the exit was wanted.
A worker running from source asks the server for no version and downloads none.
A worker running from source runs the checkout it was started in.
Every kind of file the watcher knows is watched by one loop over the kinds.
The file name a watch is logged under is read off the path the config names.
The name a handler is given is read off that file name.
A file that is absent is warned about.
A file that is absent is left unwatched.
No file present to watch answers an exit.
Every collaborator that reaches outside this module is handed in.
The clock is handed in.
The call that watches a file for changes is handed in.
The call that repeats the hourly update check is handed in.
The queue that runs uploads in turn is handed in.
The checkout the running version is read from is named by the caller.
Nothing here moves the checkout the worker runs from.
The state the watcher remembers about each file is made afresh on every start.
The running version is worked out once at startup.
An update check within a minute of the previous check does nothing.
Stopping unwatches every file watched.
Stopping halts the hourly update check.
Stopping leaves the process running.
A session naming no account answers an exit rather than signing anyone in.
The server address is read from the environment only where a session is already valid.
The startup inventory sync names the file the content was read from.
The startup inventory sync names the modification time of that file.
A fatal report is built as text rather than written anywhere.
Nothing here installs a signal handler.
Nothing here decides which account a run outcome is reported under.
The worker module hands this module a dispatch.
The worker module hands this module the session the account is read from.
The worker module beside this module builds and runs this module.
The worker the systemd unit starts is the worker module beside this module.

definition: the startup of a watcher worker, from signing in to watching every saved-variables file
